description: A never-before-seen inbound reply on a thread with exactly one registered matter, from a recorded party, is ACCEPTed on THREAD basis with a deterministic communication_id and a freshly computed ingress fingerprint.
why_it_exists: Before the round trip was built (QA workflow created 2026-08-21), communication_id was regenerated per run (WF4's pre-F-02 equivalent stamped ids with $now), so the id in the Telegram notice did not match the id written to the sheet. The resolver now derives communication_id as 'COM-' + provider_message_id so first delivery, replay and the owner notice all name the same row.

expect.ingress_fingerprint_spec: ingressFingerprint(e) = 'ING-' + fnv1a32(parts) + '-' + canon(e.body).length, where parts = ['pmid=' + trim(pmid), 'thread=' + trim(thread_id), 'from=' + emailOf(from), 'subject=' + canon(subject), 'body=' + canon(body), 'ts=' + trim(received_at)].join(' '); canon collapses all whitespace runs to a single space and trims; emailOf extracts the address inside angle brackets and lowercases it; fnv1a32 is a single 32-bit FNV-1a pass (offset basis 0x811c9dc5) rendered as 8 lowercase hex characters.
expect._correction_2026-08-25: expect.ingress_fingerprint was the prose "computed, not asserted literally". Replaced by the sentinel REGENERATE, which harness/run.js resolves through the INDEPENDENT ingressFingerprint in harness/oracles.js (never through the unit). The spec in ingress_fingerprint_spec is unchanged and is what oracles.js implements.

assertions: A thread with exactly one distinct matter_id across OUTBOUND/OUTBOUND_PENDING/INBOUND rows resolves that matter on basis THREAD.
The sender address, extracted from 'Name <addr>' and lowercased, must appear as the recipient of at least one real OUTBOUND row on that matter, or the decision is BLOCKED/SENDER_NOT_A_PARTY.
communication_id is exactly 'COM-' + provider_message_id and is not derived from a clock, a counter, or randomness.
ingress_fingerprint matches /^ING-[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9]+$/ and its trailing segment equals the whitespace-canonicalised body length (20 for 'First delivery body.').
The resolver performs no I/O, reads no clock, and is a pure function of (event, register).
